ARM agent pools and Karpenter NodePool CRDs are different. Dynamic NAP CPU/memory limits, static replicas/limits.nodes, Azure quota and pod constraints require different actions.
The AKS window controls when NAP picks up a new image; drift logic and node/pod disruption budgets control replacement. These decisions are separate from ordinary node-image channel assumptions.
Overlay allocates per-node pod CIDR blocks; pod CIDR exhaustion differs from VNet subnet exhaustion or Azure VM quota. Expansion must meet platform and superset constraints.
Eviction TooManyRequests due to zero disruptions is not an ARM throttle. Extra replicas help some budgets, but not every percentage/zero-unavailability policy.

scenarios.question: Is a ReadyToUse disk snapshot enough to recover the database consistently?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Quiesce writes using the application's supported protocol, snapshot the correct volume, restore a new consumer and validate application/data consistency rather than snapshot metadata alone.
scenarios.negative_control: Snapshot during uncontrolled writes and declare application consistency.

scenarios.question: Why do idle nodes remain after lowering the autoscaler maximum?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Use requests/allocatable rather than CPU usage alone; inspect move feasibility, PDB/safe-to-evict/local storage and timers; distinguish scale-up cap from scale-down eligibility.
scenarios.negative_control: Force node deletion or assume maxCount enforces unconditional shrink.

scenarios.question: Does our vault configuration really protect every PV against regional failure?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Join PV driver/class and disk size/access/DES fields; separate Operational/Vault tier, paired-region restore and secondary RPO.
scenarios.negative_control: Call every CSI volume eligible, conflate four-hour snapshots with Vault RPO or weaken security to pass eligibility.

scenarios.question: A supported recovery point exists, so why does target restore validation fail?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Separate extension identity, vault identity, trusted access, target/snapshot/staging scopes and restore-tier roles; validate before starting and preserve security constraints.
scenarios.negative_control: Grant subscription Owner or repeatedly restart restore without checking its named principal/scope.

scenarios.question: Why is the pod subnet full when visible pod IP use looks low?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Separate node/pod subnets; account for per-node 16-address allocations, refill below eight free, surge and churn before comparing NNC allocations to apparent demand.
scenarios.negative_control: Use Overlay /24-per-node arithmetic or count only Running pods.

scenarios.question: Why does custom DNS work directly or briefly but not persist through normal pod resolution?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Use coredns-custom import suffixes, preserve main/legacy config, reload and verify affected plus preserved query paths.
scenarios.negative_control: Edit managed Corefile, use an unimported suffix, omit process reload or verify only direct upstream.

scenarios.question: How do we migrate in-tree volumes without creating empty replacement disks?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Set Retain before logical object removal; preserve physical disk handle, prebind replacement CSI PV/PVC and verify data/consumer continuity.
scenarios.negative_control: Delete a Delete-policy claim first or create an unrelated dynamically provisioned disk.

scenarios.question: Can this existing PVC grow beyond 4 TiB without downtime?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Branch on actual disk SKU, detach when required, grow existing claim, restore consumer and verify mounted filesystem/data without recreation.
scenarios.negative_control: Treat all disk types as online or take unnecessary downtime for Premium v2.

scenarios.question: A retained LRS disk will not attach after a zone change; should we just edit node labels?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Compare actual disk zone and eligible capacity; preserve truthful topology and data, choose a same-zone pool or approved storage migration instead of falsifying labels/affinity.
scenarios.negative_control: Relabel a physical zone or remove PV affinity to pretend cross-zone LRS attachment works.

scenarios.question: Why does Azure Files still fail after its Kubernetes secret was updated?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Classify DNS/TCP445 versus SMB auth/cipher failure, verify key version without disclosing it and resolve stale mount/consumer lifecycle through an approved remount path.
scenarios.negative_control: Rotate working credentials for a network timeout or declare success from Secret metadata alone.

scenarios.question: Why does a successful live patch revert, and how do we make the repair durable?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Trace field ownership to Flux source/path, modify the approved repository overlay, reconcile and verify revision; restore any authorized temporary suspension and avoid prune-driven data loss.
scenarios.negative_control: Leave reconciliation suspended or edit only live resources.

scenarios.question: HPA reports missing CPU requests although the application container has them; why?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Inspect admitted pod and every container, including injected sidecars, then distinguish resource metric denominator problems from provider/RBAC errors.
scenarios.negative_control: Reinstall metrics-server or increase node capacity without checking actual container requests.

scenarios.question: A new routing object exists but traffic still reaches the old controller; what is missing?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Identify actual ingress/Gateway ownership, listener/parent attachment and backend readiness, preserve old routes and verify hostname/TLS/path before authorized DNS cutover.
scenarios.negative_control: Delete existing routing or switch DNS based only on resource creation.

scenarios.question: Which certificate failed, and would rotating the cluster CA cause avoidable downtime?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Distinguish serving/client/CA identities, inspect actual expiry/signer/rotation state and choose supported component-specific action; do not approve arbitrary CSRs or rotate the whole cluster blindly.
scenarios.negative_control: Disable TLS verification or treat every x509 error as expired cluster CA.

scenarios.question: Are unhealthy LB backends evidence of broken nodes when externalTrafficPolicy is Local?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Join ready local endpoint placement, healthCheckNodePort and Azure probe behavior; distinguish expected nonserving-node probe failure from a real probe/path fault without losing source IP.
scenarios.negative_control: Switch to Cluster just to make probes green or declare every nonlocal node broken.

scenarios.question: Why can our old Azure Linux pool no longer scale even though Kubernetes still runs?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Pin retirement dates and supported OS/Kubernetes/FIPS matrix; distinguish node-image refresh from OS SKU migration, stage workload validation and preserve rollback feasibility.
scenarios.negative_control: Assume a node-image-only update necessarily moves to a supported OS major version.

scenarios.question: Can we move to NAT Gateway without breaking API access or external allowlists?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Use actual managed/BYO migration matrix, associate required egress resources, update allowlists/authorized IPs and plan disruption/verification before cutover.
scenarios.negative_control: Assume public egress IP is preserved or choose a managed-VNet-only mode on BYO networking.

scenarios.question: Why did enabling Private Link PROXY protocol break otherwise healthy Local-service probes?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Check PROXY-header support of the actual health endpoint, distinguish kube-proxy health port from app probes and configure an authorized compatible probe/receiver pair.
scenarios.negative_control: Assume Local /healthz supports PROXY headers or change direct managed-LB configuration.

scenarios.question: Why are Spot pools ignored even with a priority expander?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Verify exact group-name regex coverage, priority ordering and fallback eligibility using current pool identities rather than copying ambiguous sample priorities.
scenarios.negative_control: Reverse higher/lower priority or leave the intended node group unmatched.

scenarios.question: Can we recover a Released retained PV after a claim was accidentally deleted?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Verify Retain and disk/data identity, resolve the old claim reservation, explicitly bind the new claim and verify content without deleting the physical asset.
scenarios.negative_control: Assume same claim name means same UID or permit a default class to provision new storage.

scenarios.question: Can we extend service address capacity without recreating a supported cluster?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Gate on supported version/allocator and address plan; add ServiceCIDR, preserve existing IPAddress ownership and verify new allocation; distinguish extension from moving the original service range.
scenarios.negative_control: Mutate immutable original range or delete a range still containing live service IPs.

scenarios.question: How many outbound IPs and per-node ports do we need at maximum scale, including upgrades?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Round per-node ports to eight, include all pool maxima and approved concurrent surge, size 64000-port frontends and update the AKS owner rather than its reconciled LB.
scenarios.negative_control: Fit current nodes only or edit generated outbound rule.

scenarios.question: Why does one pool's upgrade fail for another subnet?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Inventory every pool/subnet, distinguish CNI modes, use applicable maxima and surge, account for reserved/other addresses, and select an authorized feasible upgrade envelope.
scenarios.negative_control: Apply legacy maxPods formula to Overlay or inspect only the upgraded pool.

scenarios.question: Deployments are blocked by a webhook; can we recover without globally disabling enforcement?
scenarios.missing_procedure: Read matched webhook rules, service endpoints, TLS and tunnel evidence, then restore the failing relationship or use an explicitly approved narrow exception with rollback.
scenarios.negative_control: Set every failurePolicy to Ignore or assume a healthy pod proves API-server reachability.
